response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), s AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM c), a AS (SELECT c.cnt, s.avg_cnt, s.total_cnt FROM c, s WHERE c.cnt > s.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(cnt * 1.0 / total_cnt) AS avg_share_of_total, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM a

assumptions.assumption: Records with NULL college_id form a single group; GROUP BY puts NULLs together, so this is handled naturally. If no such rows exist, there is no effect.
Every row counts, so COUNT(*) is used and not COUNT of distinct players.
